{
  "screen_decision": "exclude",
  "screen_rationale": "The study reviews animal and in vitro models of autism spectrum disorder but does not report any quantitative measure of agreement or concordance between animal model results and human clinical outcomes. It focuses on the strengths and weaknesses of different models rather than their predictive accuracy.",
  "arm": "methods-and-bias",
  "arm_evidence": "Here we review the genetic and environmental risk factors for ASD and how those are modeled in animals as well as hPSC-derived 2D and 3D models. We highlight the strengths and weaknesses of each model and advocate for orthogonal validation across different model systems while also hedging claims to what a certain ASD model can unequivocally establish.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "psychiatric",
    "neurodegeneration"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders (NDDs and NPDs) impose an ever-increasing burden on global health today [ 1 , 2 ].",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "Animals such as rats and mice have traditionally been used to model ASD phenotypes... Over the last decade, human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived 2D models such as induced neurons (iNs) as well as 3D models (organoids, assembloids) have started to bridge this gap.",
  "species": [
    "mouse",
    "rat",
    "pig",
    "non-human-primate"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "A variety of animals have been used to model ASD phenotypes [ 169 , 176 , 184 , 185 , 186 , 187 , 188 , 189 , 190 , 191 , 192 , 193 ], of which mice, rats, pigs, and non-human primates are discussed below.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "Common behavioral tests employed for the evaluation of ASD-like behaviors in mice include the three-chambered assay for sociability, ultrasonic vocalization for communication, marble burying for stereotypy, and the T-maze or Morris water maze for spatial memory as well as cognitive flexibility [ 177 , 178 ]."
}
